days.title: Western Coast and Heights
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Keem Bay
stops.detail: Keem Bay (Irish: Trá na Coime) in the far west near Achill Head is considered one of Ireland's most beautiful beaches.

stops.name: Cliffs of Croaghaun
stops.detail: Those who wish to catch a glimpse of the highest cliffs in Ireland, not yet developed for tourism (Cliffs of Croaghaun), must undertake the quite steep ascent (without designated paths) onto the grass-covered Achill Head.

days.title: Northern History and Monuments
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Keel East
stops.detail: Keel East is a megalithic complex built on Achill during the 4th and 3rd millennia BC in the Neolithic.

stops.name: Deserted Village
stops.detail: The ruined village of Deserted Village (Irish: Baile Tréigthe) is located in the north on the foothills of the 671 m high Slievemore.

stops.name: Achill-henge
stops.detail: Achill-henge refers to a massive round concrete structure made of 30 columns about four meters high with a circumference of more than 100 m, which resembles Stonehenge.

days.title: Southern Shores and Islands

stops.name: Atlantic Drive
stops.detail: The Atlantic Drive (Irish: Bóthar an Atlantaigh) in the south and west of the island offers many impressive, partly wind-prone viewpoints of the island, bays, and the Atlantic surf, such as at Camport Bay, a bay located southeast of Dooega.

stops.name: Kildavnet Tower
stops.detail: In the 16th century, Grace O’Malley maintained a castle near Kildavnet (Kildavnet Tower, Irish: Túr Chill Dhamhnait) on the island.
